question.text: Per NISM-Series-IV workbook pp. 276-277, which set of statutes is identified as forming the core statutory basis for the exchange-traded interest rate derivatives (ETIRD) market in India (underlying G-Secs, SEBI's regulatory mandate, and securities contracts framework)?

answer.text: Government Securities Act 2006, SEBI Act 1992, and SC(R)A 1956
RBI Act 1934, Companies Act 2013, and SEBI Act 1992
Banking Regulation Act 1949, FEMA 1999, and SC(R)A 1956
SEBI Act 1992, Income Tax Act 1961, and RBI Act 1934

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook pages cited list (a) the Government Securities Act 2006 — governs the underlying G-Secs, (b) the SEBI Act 1992 — gives SEBI authority over exchanges and derivatives, and (c) the SC(R)A 1956 — provides the legal framework for securities contracts and derivatives. Together these are the core statutes underpinning the ETIRD market on the dimensions named in the stem. The Trap: The original stem asked for "the three main legislations", but the workbook actually lists a wider statutory framework that also includes the RBI Act 1934, Banking Regulation Act 1949, and the Depositories Act, alongside exchange/clearing bye-laws. That made the original ambiguous — options like "RBI Act 1934, Companies Act 2013, and SEBI Act 1992" become partly defensible if "main" is read loosely. Companies Act, FEMA, and Income Tax Act are not part of the ETIRD statutory framework. Note: The original stem implied an exhaustive list of "the three main" laws, which the workbook does not state. The stem has been narrowed to ask which set of three statutes covers the three specific dimensions (underlying G-Secs / SEBI mandate / securities contracts framework), uniquely supporting option A. RBI Act 1934 and Banking Regulation Act 1949 also appear in the workbook framework but cover different dimensions (NISM-Series-IV pp. 276-277).
